picked.t: Japan looks to Bangladesh, Nepal for farmhands as Vietnamese recruiters struggle to fill jobs
picked.body: Tokyo-based Mirai, which trains and places skilled foreign workers, has introduced its first Bangladeshi candidates for farm work, Kyodo News reported. Two students from one of its partner schools in Bangladesh passed Japan's specified skilled worker agriculture exam in August and received job offers from an agricultural company in northeastern Aomori Prefecture, where they are due to head in the coming months. "I am very excited to go to Japan and learn about Japanese agriculture," Ahasan Habib, 21, from Mymensingh in northern Bangladesh, told the Japanese news site. "I want to make good use of my experience and take proper care of chickens." The other candidate, Siam Ur Rahman, 20, from Barisal in southern Bangladesh, said he wanted "to work very hard" in Japan and was looking forward to touching snow. The two will join Japan's Type 1 specified skilled workers in agriculture, whose stays are generally capped at five years. Their number rose 26% from a year earlier to 44,050 at the end of June, according to the Immigration Services Agency. Indonesia remained the largest supplier with 18,255 farm workers, up 45%, followed by Vietnam with 10,261, up 11%. Vietnam's share of the sector fell from about 26% a year earlier to 23%, although it is still the largest source of Type 1 workers across all fields, with 163,154 of the 425,961 in Japan. South Asian farm workers numbers remain small but are climbing fast. Bangladesh's count jumped 127% to 334, Sri Lanka's climbed 60% to 638 and Nepal's rose 30% to 916. Yuji Nomura, general manager of the career advisory division at Mirai's parent company Sustainable Holdings, told Kyodo News that rising wages in Vietnam, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries were making it harder for Japan to attract farm workers from there. "We're seeing a shift to South Asia for labor supply sources," he said. To qualify for specified skilled worker status in agriculture, candidates should pass the N4 beginner-level Japanese test as well as written and practical farming exams, Nomura said. Sustainable Holdings runs Mirai partner schools in the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and has added schools in Sri Lanka and Nepal. Japan's farms face chronic labor shortages due to aging and other factors. Including technical intern trainees, 67,905 foreigners held specified skilled worker or trainee status in agriculture at the end of 2025, according to government data. Noriyuki Takakura, a director at Sustainable Holdings, said workers from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal were highly regarded for their seriousness and diligence. The company offers free tuition at Mirai partner schools across Asia and helps students find housing in Japan. "We will gradually expand agricultural classes in each country," Takakura said. In Vietnam, Japan was the top destination for workers going abroad in 2025, receiving more than 64,600, but it has slipped to second place this year. Of the 114,276 Vietnamese who left to work overseas on contracts in the first 10 months, 50,473 went to Taiwan and 45,658 to Japan, according to the Department of Overseas Labor Management. Pham Van Trong, human resources manager at a Hanoi company that has sent workers to Japan for more than a decade, including in agriculture, told VnExpress that each job order once drew seven or eight applicants but now gets about two per position. The company's supply of candidates has fallen about 60%, he said. Trong said more jobs at home were part of the reason, with unskilled construction work now paying around VND20 million ($770). But he blamed mainly the weaker yen, which once fetched VND200-220 and now fetches about VND160-170. Workers' total incomes are 1.2 to 1.5 times what they were a decade ago, but their savings have not kept pace. On VND30-40 million ($1,150-1,540) a month, they used to send home VND20-25 million ($770-960), and they still send about the same. "With the yen sliding and savings not growing, workers will think twice," Trong said.

picked.t: Crowded trains and full parking lots mark HCMC metro's 2nd year
picked.body: Around 8 a.m. on Nov. 26, passengers packed the platform at National University Station waiting for a train to Ben Thanh. It is one of the busiest stops along Metro Line 1, or Ben Thanh - Suoi Tien, with students accounting for the majority of riders. The line started running in December 2024, spanning more than 20 km between Ben Thanh in HCMC's center and Suoi Tien in the city's east. Nguyen Van Long, deputy head of the Transport Management Division under the HCMC Department of Construction, Metro Line 1 operated nearly 73,000 trips in the first 10 months of 2026. The line served about 20.25 million passengers, a 21% year-on-year increase, averaging more than 66,600 riders daily. Ridership surges during the morning and evening rush hours. Station attendants remain positioned at carriage doors, continuously urging passengers to disembark quickly and clear the way for boarding commuters so trains can depart on schedule. In September, each train carried an average of 750 passengers during peak hours. By October, the line was handling roughly 5,700 riders every 30 minutes across both directions during rush hour. During peak periods, crowds surge from the platforms into packed carriages as soon as a train pulls in. "In the morning, passenger volume is heaviest heading into the city center, and in the afternoon, it's the reverse," said commuter Nguyen Hoang Anh. The operator said it is calculating adjustments to train frequencies, with priority given to peak hours. Longer term, the city is considering acquiring additional rolling stock to run six-car trains and expand capacity. picked.t: Inside Binh Tay, the 96-year-old Chinatown market in HCMC
picked.body: Binh Tay Market is situated between Thap Muoi, Le Tan Ke, Phan Van Khoe, and Tran Binh streets in Binh Tay Ward, an area with a large Hoa community, people of Chinese ancestry. Besides serving locals, the market is a regular stop for tourists visiting HCMC. According to Nguyen Thi Ngoc Chau, deputy director of the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market was built in 1930. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. Quach Dam, a Chinese-born merchant, funded the market's construction. His bust stands in the atrium at the center of the market, and is also regarded as the "God of Wealth" for local traders. Every day, vendors and others who make a living at the market come to burn incense and pray for good business. The market, which was renovated in 2016, retains its original architecture. It spreads over 25,000 square meters with a floor area of more than 17,000 square meters, and has one main gate and 12 side entrances. It has a tall tower with four clock faces. The yin-yang tiled roofs are arranged in overlapping layers and curve upward at the corners. In 2017, the market was recognized as a city architectural and artistic heritage site. In 2022, it was named a tourist attraction of HCMC. According to Le Hong Minh, head of the business management team at the Binh Tay Ward Public Service Center, the market has 2,358 stalls that sell more than 30 product categories. Its main goods include spices, groceries, clothing, and confectionery. Data from 2023 to 2026 shows that 73% of visitors to the market are international. It receives 120,000 foreign visitors a year, most of them brought on guided tours. On Sept. 8, a group of 10 Indian tourists led by Rohan and his wife spent over an hour exploring the market and buying more than a dozen handmade bags as gifts. Rohan praised its architecture and range of goods but said the products were similar to those at other markets in town. Stalls selling dry goods and spices are located near the market's main gate. Minh said shopping preferences at Binh Tay vary by region. European and American tourists buy handicrafts and clothing. Southeast Asian visitors shop for confectionery, tea, coffee, and bamboo goods. Northeast Asian tourists prefer specialties, dried foods, and herbal medicines. Besides shopping, the market has a food area serving dishes from all over Vietnam. Binh Tay Market plans to combine shopping with cultural and culinary experiences by offering heritage tours, spiritual visits, performances recreating old Chinatown, craft workshops with artisans, and Chinese-Vietnamese cuisine. picked.t: British tourist couple amazed by 20-minute hospital visit in Ha Giang
picked.body: While traveling through Vietnam's northern mountains from Cao Bang to Ha Giang in northern Vietnam in October, 31-year-old Katie had a painful swelling in her leg. Worried about an infection, she and her boyfriend Ryan, 34, went to Duc Minh Ha Giang General Hospital on Oct. 23. Because neither spoke Vietnamese, he used Google Translate to communicate with the staff. Katie was admitted quickly and taken straight to a treatment room where a doctor spent 10 minutes draining, cleaning, and bandaging the swelling, using a translation app to explain every step. When it was done and she picked up her medication, only 20 minutes had elapsed from the time they had entered. "We were genuinely surprised by how fast it was," Ryan said. It was their third trip to Vietnam, and neither had ever needed medical care before. At first, they were worried about long lines, high costs, and the language barrier. He said in the U.K. patients often wait 5 to 10 hours to see a doctor. He had also heard stories about foreigners getting hit with massive medical bills in Vietnam, and so was relieved by how affordable the treatment was. The two quit their jobs in 2023 to travel the world on their savings and have visited 39 countries so far. They returned to Vietnam in September for a 44-day trip through Hanoi, Ha Giang, Cao Bang, and Ninh Binh. Along with the scenery, food, and friendly locals, the helpful hospital staff also left a lasting impression on them. Dr. Truong Viet Anh, director of Duc Minh Ha Giang General Hospital, said the emergency team treated Katie after regular hours for a minor skin infection (a soft-tissue abscess) on her lower right leg. Since the procedure was simple, the staff easily communicated using translation apps on their phones. He said the hospital gets 120 to 150 foreign tourists each month, mostly for injuries, digestive disorders, viral fevers, or sore throats. The hospital uses a public price list and always discloses costs before starting treatment, but language, payment options, and travel insurance paperwork are constant challenges, he said. "We are working to improve our staff's foreign language skills and creating a bilingual documentation system." Looking at the bigger picture for medical tourism in Vietnam, Dr. Mai Van Dien, director of An Sinh Hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, said short wait times and prices that are 50-70% lower than in Singapore or Japan give the country a big advantage. Many foreign patients fly to Vietnam because they can get surgery in one or two weeks instead of waiting months at home. But the low prices must be backed by high-quality care to keep patients coming back, he said. Dr. Jean-Marcel Guillon, CEO of FV Hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, agreed. He said while Vietnam's medical expertise, transportation, and tourism services are improving, hospitals must focus on language support, clear pricing, and consistent service to earn the trust of international patients.

picked.t: 8 tidal gates shield Ho Chi Minh City streets from flooding
picked.body: Tran Xuan Soan Street in former District 7 remained dry at 5:30 p.m., despite being a regular flooding hotspot whenever water levels in nearby rivers and canals rise. Just a month earlier, a stretch of more than 3 km of the road was submerged, with floodwaters reaching halfway up vehicle wheels and forcing many commuters to push their motorbikes through the water. The road's protection from flooding is attributed to the newly completed VND10 trillion (US$387 million) tidal control system. At noon on Wednesday, project investor Trung Nam Group lowered the sluice gates, closing all eight tidal control structures at the mouths of major rivers in the city's urban core. The system has helped reduce high-tide flooding in several areas in the city's south, including parts of the former districts 1, 7 and 8, and Nha Be District. The project is expected to mitigate flooding across 570 sq.km of the inner city, equivalent to one-fourth of the city’s land area before the merger, benefiting approximately 6.5 million people. picked.t: Nutifood forms US nutrition science alliance with four partners
picked.body: Nutifood announced the establishment of Nutifood American Nutrition Science in Kansas on Nov. 24. The new entity will connect the company's research and product development capabilities with the U.S. nutrition science, dairy ingredients, and manufacturing sectors. The launch was marked by a signing ceremony with Dairy Farmers of America (DFA), witnessed by representatives of the Vietnamese Consulate General in San Francisco and senior U.S. dairy industry executives. Building on a scientific foundation The move builds on Nutifood's more than 25 years of research and development (R&D) experience across Vietnam, Sweden, and Australia, where it has developed nutrition solutions for different consumer needs. In early 2026, the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) granted a patent for the company's proprietary FDI formula, expanding its intellectual property portfolio. The U.S. offers an opportunity for Nutifood to tap into an advanced dairy ecosystem spanning ingredients, manufacturing, research, and clinical science. Through its new entity, the company aims to combine its intellectual property and research expertise with U.S. scientific and industrial resources, moving beyond conventional exports to participate more deeply in the nutrition value chain. Four U.S. partners Nutifood is forming a Nutrition Science Alliance with the California Milk Advisory Board (CMAB), California Dairies, Inc. (CDI), DFA, and Natural Immune Systems Laboratories (NIS Labs). Each partner brings different capabilities: CMAB connects the company with California's dairy industry and products bearing the Real California Milk seal; CDI provides large-scale dairy processing and manufacturing; DFA contributes R&D and formula innovation; and NIS Labs offers laboratory testing, preclinical studies, and human research. By combining these capabilities across ingredients, manufacturing, R&D, and clinical research, Nutifood aims to improve control over product development and meet scientific and quality standards in international markets. "Every age group, body condition, and stage of life requires specialized nutrition solutions grounded in scientific evidence. That is why Nutifood American Nutrition Science is not simply looking for ingredient suppliers or manufacturing facilities in the United States," said Tran Bao Minh, vice chairman of Nutifood. "We are building strategic partnerships with CMAB, CDI, DFA, and NIS Labs to combine advanced technology and research capabilities in order to develop new nutrition standards for consumers worldwide." Through its U.S. entity and four strategic partnerships, Nutifood aims to strengthen its international competitiveness by combining its research capabilities and patented technologies with American scientific and manufacturing resources.

picked.t: Vietnam's growing affection for pets challenges longstanding dog and cat meat trade
picked.body: Phuong is here because he's seen many ‌stories in Facebook groups of owners finding missing pets at markets like this one. "There is a high chance that Dom was stolen," the 40-year-old ceramics trader says of the cat he raised from a kitten. She has never gone missing before, he says, and several neighbors also lost pets the same night. Pet theft rings Vietnamese police report detaining scores of suspected pet thieves this year, accused of stealing thousands of cats and dogs to sell for slaughter. Last month, Ho Chi Minh City police arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats destined for the meat trade. In April, Hanoi police arrested five people over the theft of more than 300 cats. Criminals tend ⁠to operate late at night, riding on motorcycles and carrying sacks, duct tape and makeshift weapons, including improvised stun guns, to subdue the animals, according to the reports. Clash of cultures The criminals are operating at the nexus of a cultural shift in the country of 100 million people, drawn largely along generational lines. Younger Vietnamese increasingly view dogs and cats as pets, and Hanoi's municipal government has made efforts to curb the trade in dog and cat meat to align with global norms. However, the meat remains on menus around the country, and whole roasted dogs can be seen in street stalls in parts of the capital. Rising pet ownership has provided thieves with more targets, which can be sold into a well-established meat trade. Prices vary widely, but a live dog fetches around $1.50 per kg (68 cents per pound), while a cat goes for closer to $5 per kg, according to the police reports. "Cat meat is a favorite dish for working-class people," said Tran Thanh, a 50-year-old truck driver from Hai Phong. "Mostly people of my age or older keep the habit," he said, explaining that for about $23 a group of half a dozen people can share a cat-meat hot pot. "We choose cat meat instead ‌of pork or ⁠chicken because it goes well with rice wine." Eating dog and cat meat has a long history in Vietnam, with some believing the meat boosts vitality or wards off bad luck. There are no official figures on the size of the market, but animal welfare group Four Paws International in a 2020 report estimated that over 5 million dogs and 1 million cats were slaughtered annually. However, shifting attitudes have taken a toll on the industry, which has witnessed a steady, years-long decline. "Young people nowadays keep dogs indoors and treat them like members of the family," said Tran Huu Thanh, a 70-year-old former dog meat restaurant owner, who shut his business in 2019 after sales dropped significantly. Hanoi's government in 2018 urged residents to stop eating the meat, saying ⁠it tarnishes the city's image and facilitates the spread of rabies. Last year, it launched a pilot programme aimed at encouraging dog and cat meat traders to move into other professions by providing vocational training. The finance ministry-run Vietnam Investment Review reported this week that a year into the initiative, 28 businesses had made the switch. Open-air trade By law, vendors are required to show proof of origin for the animals they sell, but Hanoi locals say enforcement is lax. Three of the five stall operators at ⁠a wet market in the city approached by Reuters said they did not know where their animals came from. All declined to give their names. Hanoi's largest sanctuary for abandoned and stolen pets, SNNC Dog and Cat Rescue Center, sometimes gets phone calls from people about animals being transported to slaughterhouses. Workers will often intervene to buy them for more money than their meat ⁠will fetch, said Phan Trung Thanh, who volunteers as communications manager for the non-profit group. But he said SNNC has had to cut back on the number of rescues because it lacks the funds to take in more than the roughly 1,400 animals already at the sanctuary. Meanwhile, Phuong still has not found his cat, a month after she went missing. He continues to monitor internet sites where he says people post photos of animals, seeking payment for their return. "Dom was my emotional support," he said. "The house is empty without her."

picked.t: [단독] 신한은행베트남, 긴급점검에 온라인뱅킹 돌연 ‘먹통’…"지갑 없이 나왔는데 밥값도 못 내"
picked.body: 신한은행베트남 호치민시 푸미흥 지점 내부.  27일 신한베트남은행이 긴급 시스템 점검을 이유로 온라인뱅킹 서비스를 중단했다. 이날 오전 신한베트남은행은 긴급 시스템 점검으로 온라인뱅킹 서비스 이용이 일시적으로 중단된다는 문자 메시지를 자사 고객들에게 발송했다. 은행 측에 따르면, 카드 결제나 ATM 서비스 및 창구 거래는 가능하다. 신한은행은 이날 베트남 전 지점 영업시간을 오후 7시로 연장하고, 지점 송금 수수료를 면제한다고 밝혔다. 평소 창구 영업이 오후 4시 30분까지인 것을 감안하면 두 시간 반을 더 여는 것이다. 현재 신한베트남은행 공식 홈페이지에는 시스템 개선으로 27일부터 온라인뱅킹 서비스가 중단된다는 팝업 알림창이 출력되고 있다. 단, 서비스 정상화 시점은 구체적으로 명시되지 않았다. 통상 계획된 점검은 시작 및 종료 시각이 사전에 안내되는 것을 감안하면 이례적인 상황으로 풀이된다. 27일 신한베트남은행이 고객들에게 발송한 안내문. 현재 신한베트남은행의 뱅킹앱 ‘쏠(SOL)’ 역시 로그인이 불가능한 상태다. 이로 인해 현지 교민과 자영업자는 큰 불편을 호소하고 있다. QR코드를 통한 계좌이체가 일상화된 만큼, 은행앱이 열리지 않으면 마트에서 음료수를 사거나 식사값을 치르는 사소한 소비활동마저 불가능하기 때문이다. 실제로 이날 오전 교민들이 모인 온라인 단체 대화방에는 앱 오류를 묻는 글이 잇따랐다. "신한은행 앱이 잘 되느냐, 계속 오류가 뜬다"고 묻는 한 교민의 질문에 신한베트남은행이 보낸 알림문이 공유됐고, 이후 "지점 영업시간을 연장하는 게 의미가 있느냐, 앱을 언제 다시 쓸 수 있는지를 알려줘야 한다"는 불만과 "지갑을 안 들고 나온 사람은 난감하겠다", "하루 이틀도 아니고 툭하면 이러니 현금을 꼭 들고 다닌다", "앱만 믿기에는 불안하다"는 반응이 이어졌다. 신한베트남은행의 온라인뱅킹 중단에 불편을 호소하는 베트남 교민들의 모습. 신한은행에 앞서 KB증권 베트남법인(KBSV)에서는 이달 6일 법인 명의의 현지 은행 계좌에서 법인자금 약 414억 동(약 21억7,000만 원)이 현지 20여 개 은행의 수십 개 계좌로 분산돼 유출되는 사고가 발생했다. 한 달 사이 베트남에 진출한 한국계 금융사에서 자금 유출과 온라인 채널 중단이 겹치면서 교민들 사이 우려가 커지고 있다.

picked.t: 베트남 최대 통신社 비엣텔, ‘스타링크’ 위성인터넷 재판매 시작…월이용료 160만동
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 최대 통신회사 군대통신그룹(Viettel·비엣텔)이 스타링크(Starlink) 재판매를 통해 위성인터넷 서비스를 출시했다. 장비 가격은 930만 동(360달러), 요금은 월 159만 동부터로 장비와 첫 달 요금을 합친 금액은 1,089만 동(62달러)부터 시작한다. 비엣텔텔레콤(Viettel Telecom)은 26일 성명을 통해 자사가 판매하는 스타링크 위성인터넷 서비스요금을 발표했다. 회사 측에 따르면, 요금제는 국내용(Local)과 국제용·해상용(Global) 등 3가지 스타링크 기기 패키지로 마련됐다. 이 중 국내용 요금제는 서비스 제공 지역 내 베트남 육지와 연안 해역에서 사용이 가능하며, 국제·해상용은 먼 바다에 위치해있거나, 국제 노선을 오가는 선박에서 사용이 가능하다. 이에 대해 비엣텔텔레콤은 “4G(4세대 이동통신) 및 5G 서비스와 함께 위성인터넷이라는 새로운 연결 방식을 통해 지리적 제약과 인프라 구축 시간 제약, 지상 인프라 의존 등에 대한 한계를 극복할 수 있게 됐다”고 설명했다. 비엣텔텔레콤에 따르면, 장비 구입 가격은 930만 동부터, 요금제는 월 159만 동부터 시작한다. 장비와 첫 달 요금을 합친 금액은 최저 1,089만동이다. 비엣텔텔레콤 서비스 이용자는 사용설명서에 따라 직접 장비를 설치하거나 현장지원서비스(유료)를 신청할 수 있다. 한편, 비엣텔텔레콤은 스페이스X 직구와 자사가 판매하는 서비스의 차이점에 대해 종합 연결 솔루션을 꼽았다. 사용자에 따라 어떤 기술과 장비, 요금제가 맞는지 상담해 주는 단계부터 설치 및 사용 기간 지원을 책임진다는 설명이다. 스타링크는 저궤도 위성을 통해 케이블이나 기지국 없이 인터넷 연결 환경을 구축하는 위성인터넷 서비스다. 비엣텔에 따르면, 최적의 조건에서 다운로드 속도는 400Mbps 이상, 지연 시간은 20~50ms에 이를 수 있다. 앞서 스타링크는 지난 8월 중순 베트남 서비스를 출시한 바 있다. 사용자는 비엣텔 외 스타링크 홈페이지에서 서비스를 직접 신청할 수 있다. 한편, 비엣텔은 이번 위성인터넷 서비스 재판매로, 기존 인프라로 연결성이 제한되는 도서산간 및 외딴 지역과 먼 바다를 항해하는 선박 등 다양한 사용자군의 가입자가 유치될 것으로 기대하고 있다.

picked.t: ‘美관세 35%’ 베트남 외교부 “무역협정 사실상 마무리 단계…기술적 사안만 남아”
picked.body: 팜 투 항 베트남 외교부 대변인. (사진=베트남 외교부) 미국 행정부가 베트남에 과잉생산에 따른 35%의 고율 신규 관세 부과를 예고한 가운데, 베트남 외교부는 미국과 상호무역협정이 사실상 마무리 단계에 접어들었다며 과도한 우려에 대해 선을 그었다. 팜 투 항(Pham Thu Hang) 베트남 외교부 대변인은 26일 하노이에서 열린 정례 브리핑에서 “미국 무역대표부(USTR)의 관세 부과안은 아직 적용되지 않았으며, 최종 결정은 늦어도 2027년 3월 11일까지 나올 것으로 전망된다고 말했다. 이날 항 대변인은 미국 행정부의 최근 신규 관세 예고에 대해 베트남의 대응을 묻는 질의에 이 같이 답했다. 앞서 USTR은 지난 25일(현지시간) 무역법 제301조(섹션 301)에 따라 14개 경제권을 대상으로 과잉생산 관세 부과를 예고했다. 관세가 예고된 14개 경제권은 △한국 △베트남 △중국 △일본 △방글라데시 △캄보디아 △유럽연합(EU) △인도 △인도네시아 △말레이시아 △싱가포르 △스위스 △대만 △태국 등으로, 국가별 세율은 한국·일본·EU가 15%인 반면, 베트남은 최대 35%로 14개 경제권 가운데 가장 높다. USTR은 조사대상국이던 멕시코와 노르웨이 등 2개국을 이번 관세 대상 경제권에 포함하지 않았다. 항 대변인은 “최근 며칠 사이 이 사안이 언론의 상당한 관심을 받고 있으며, 공상부가 이미 관련 정보를 제공한 바 있다”고 답했다. 실제로 공상부는 USTR의 발표 직후 긴급 성명을 통해 “현재 대(對)미국 관세율은 잠정치일뿐이며, 곧바로 적용되는 관세율은 아니”라며 “양국 간 상호무역협정이 체결될 경우, 관세율은 20%로 내려갈 수 있다”고 밝힌 바 있다. 항 대변인은 “USTR의 잠정 결론과 제안된 최고 세율은 미국의 법적 절차의 일부”라면서도 “현재 관세율은 제안일 뿐, 곧바로 효력이 발생하는 것은 아니며, 아직 공식 시행되지도 않았다”고 강조하며 “USTR은 최종 결정 이전 각계 의견 수렴과 관련 당사자들과 협의를 거칠 예정이며, 이를 통해 적용 관세율과 관세 부과 방식, 기존 관세와의 관계, 면제 대상 품목 등이 결정될 것”이라고 했다. 베트남 호치민시 깟라이항. 항 대변인은 “베트남은 미국과 상호·공정·균형 무역협정을 협상하며 여러 약속을 이행해 왔으며, 1974년 무역법 제301조에 따른 조사와 관련된 문제를 포함해 미국이 우려하는 사안을 풀기 위해 주요 개혁도 앞서 추진했다”며 “현재 양측은 협상 내용 대부분을 사실상 마무리지은 상태로, 전체 협상을 끝내기 위해 추가적인 기술적 논의와 명확한 정리가 필요한 몇 가지 사안만 남겨둔 상태”라고 강조했다. 항 대변인은 “이러한 분야에서 베트남이 낸 노력과 성과를 미국이 객관적이고 균형 있게 평가해주길 바란다”며 “베트남은 앞으로도 선의를 바탕으로 미국 측과 직접 협의를 이어 가고, 남아 있는 이견을 원만히 해결하기 위해 정보 공유와 정책·규정 등에 대해 충분히 설명할 준비가 돼 있다”고 덧붙였다. 섹션 301은 미국의 통상 이익을 침해하거나 유해하다고 판단되는 외국 정부의 부당한 정책 및 관행에 대해 미국 정부가 자체 조사 후 높은 관세 부과 등 강력한 무역 제재를 가할 수 있도록 허용하는 조항이다. 앞서 도널드 트럼프 미국 행정부는 보조금에 따른 과잉생산으로 값싼 상품이 미국으로 밀려들어 현지 기업의 경쟁력이 약화되는 등 피해가 발생했다고 주장하며 16개 경제권을 대상으로 지난 3월 섹션301에 따른 조사를 시작한 바 있다. 이에 앞서 USTR은 지난 7월 60개 경제권을 대상으로 진행한 강제노동 조사 결과를 발표하며, 한국과 베트남 등에 10~12.5% 관세를 부과한 바 있다.
